reason: The context accepts the fixture's self-signed certificate, which Chromium refuses per context (acceptInsecureCerts is Unsupported there)
A route that handles only its first N requests (`times`) and then stops; Strider's routes have no such option, so a handler has to count its own requests

route.fallback({ url }) hands the request to the next matching route with a new URL, and chains through three routes; Route.continueWith can change the URL but never passes the request on to the next route

The port fulfills the popup's own paused response at the response phase, which Strider does on Chromium only: Firefox can't fulfill at that phase (interception.responseFulfill), and WebKit can't read a paused response's body (interception.responseBody, CDP only) nor change its headers (interception.responseHeaders). Playwright's route.fetch works on every browser
A URLPattern with ignoreCase: Strider's URL patterns are strings, and a URLPattern string has no case-insensitive option
